justification: The cooperative 'registered the Aveste mark in 2014', 'The mark is precise about equipment' and 'bars washing and heat-drying', and 212 of 340 pans (about two thirds) belong to the cooperative. A is contradicted because 'the rest are worked by two families who never joined'; B is contradicted by the mark's explicit written rules; C's motive for registration is never given.

Pella Marsa 'was floored in the 1990s to take a small harvester, and its dates are settled before the season opens'. B is explicitly rejected — 'it is not that the harvester bruises the crystal' — C describes the two Aveste families who never joined, and washing/grading (D) is never mentioned.

On chemistry 'the three relined pans behave like the clay ones', and 'Nothing her panels could find in the salt recorded the relining. The people did' — the pair 'misread the crust in both seasons' until they 'had the new floors by heart'. The change surfaced in how the pans had to be read, not in the salt; C is contradicted because the lateness stopped by 2021, and D contradicts the chemistry finding.

Panek 'disputes none of it' and Solbes 'agrees with every word of that and has said so in print', so the objection is presented as fair; yet the writer continues 'Then she points to the concrete' and closes on the mark guaranteeing a lath 'which no panel in five seasons has managed to taste' while 'nothing at Aveste writes that part down'. Fair, but not allowed to close the argument ('nobody has answered that yet'). A ends the argument, B is too cynical for a text where everyone accepts Panek's premise, and D wrongly claims Solbes largely answered it.

The closing sentence carries the thesis: the mark 'goes on guaranteeing a wooden lath, which no panel in five seasons has managed to taste', while the pan-holders decide dwell, 'which every panel can taste, and nothing at Aveste writes that part down' — the inspectable versus the recorded-nowhere judgement. A and D are contradicted ('None of which is an argument against the lath'; 'it is not that the harvester bruises the crystal'), and C's price-premium survival claim is not the text's point.

'A loaf sealed in a bag loses almost no water overnight' yet the tasters 'still mark it down by morning', and 'Nothing has left the bag; it has only moved' — staling as internal rearrangement rather than loss. C invents a disagreement (panels and scales agree with each other against the drying-out answer), and D reverses the direction: the water 'moves outwards and softens the crust' while 'the crumb stiffens'.

The passage says 'Two hundred and twelve of the pans belong to the cooperative that registered the Aveste mark in 2014' out of 'three hundred and forty pans' — about two thirds — and 'The mark is precise about equipment. It names the lath, keeps metal out of the pan, bars washing and heat-drying.' D matches all three facts. A is contradicted (128 pans sit outside the mark), B is contradicted by the mark's precision, and C's anti-neighbour motive is never stated.

Verbatim support: 'The saltern at Pella Marsa... was floored in the 1990s to take a small harvester, and its dates are settled before the season opens.' B is explicitly contradicted — 'it is not that the harvester bruises the crystal. It is that the harvester comes on a Tuesday.' C misattributes Aveste's two non-cooperative families to Pella Marsa, and D's washing and grading are never mentioned.

The passage concludes 'Nothing her panels could find in the salt recorded the relining. The people did' — the workers 'misread the crust in both seasons and lifted late' until 'they had the new floors by heart.' That is B: the change showed up in how the pans had to be read, not in the salt. C is contradicted by the lateness stopping in 2021, and D by 'On chemistry the three relined pans behave like the clay ones.'

The objection is granted as fair — 'Solbes agrees with every word of that and has said so in print' — but not allowed to end the matter: 'Then she points to the concrete,' and the closing paragraph keeps the irony alive that the mark guarantees 'a wooden lath, which no panel in five seasons has managed to taste.' A fails because the writer does not leave the craft question there; B is too cynical since the committee 'has not refused it either' and asks a question 'nobody has answered'; D fails because the inspector problem is the core objection and remains unanswered.

The main idea is stated in Panek's 'You can photograph a lath... You cannot photograph a decision about whether the crust is ready' and sealed by the final sentence: the mark guarantees the lath while pan-holders work out 'whether today is the day... and nothing at Aveste writes that part down.' A overreaches ('None of which is an argument against the lath'), C's price-survival claim is background only, and D is contradicted — 'it is not that the harvester bruises the crystal.'

The text's own headline claim is 'Nothing has left the bag; it has only moved' — a sealed loaf 'loses almost no water overnight' yet stales, because water 'moves outwards and softens the crust' while the crumb stiffens. That is B: rearrangement rather than loss. C distorts (tasters and scales agree with each other, against the folk answer 'it dries out'), and D reverses the direction of the water and the fate of the crumb.
